args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 production deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened incident INC-0001 as a SEV2, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The service was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to it didn't need approval, because it has been healthy in production before.
- **After:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 on checkout-api. It covers the failed deploy, the rollback and the result. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's redeployed.

The test build of v2.3.1 was already failing health checks in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. Whoever looks into the cause should check why it was promoted anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
